definitions.gloss: to whistle (with one's lips); to whistle a tune
definitions.explanation: To make a whistling sound by blowing air through puckered lips, often while doing something casually or carefree. Can be whistling a tune or just whistling for expression, for calling, or absentmindedly. The standard Japanese way to describe whistling.

examples.japanese: {口笛|くちぶえ}を{吹|ふ}きながら{歩|ある}く。
{彼|かれ}は{機嫌|きげん}がいいとき、いつも{口笛|くちぶえ}を{吹|ふ}く。
examples.english: He always whistles when he's in a good mood.

examples.japanese: {父|ちち}は{車|くるま}を{洗|あら}いながら、{好|す}きな{曲|きょく}の{口笛|くちぶえ}を{吹|ふ}いていた。
examples.english: My father was whistling his favorite tune while washing the car.

examples.japanese: {夜|よる}に{口笛|くちぶえ}を{吹|ふ}くと{蛇|へび}が{来|く}るという{言|い}い{伝|つた}えを、{子供|こども}のころ{祖母|そぼ}から{聞|き}いたことがある。
examples.english: When I was a child, I heard from my grandmother the folk belief that if you whistle at night, snakes will come.

notes:
Composed of {口笛|くちぶえ} (whistle, literally "mouth flute") and {吹|ふ}く (to blow). The standard way to say "to whistle" in Japanese — the verb {吹|ふ}く (to blow) is used because whistling is produced by blowing air, and {口笛|くちぶえ} is treated as the instrument being played.

USAGE:
This phrase is almost always used as {口笛|くちぶえ}を{吹|ふ}く with the particle を. It can describe:
- whistling a tune: {好|す}きな{歌|うた}の{口笛|くちぶえ}を{吹|ふ}く
- whistling absentmindedly or cheerfully
- whistling to call someone or a dog (though this is less common in Japan than in some cultures)

CULTURAL NOTE:
There is a well-known folk superstition that whistling at night brings snakes, thieves, or other misfortune — {夜|よる}に{口笛|くちぶえ}を{吹|ふ}くと{蛇|へび}が{来|く}る (or どろぼう — thieves). Many older Japanese were told this as children and still avoid whistling after dark out of habit.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {口笛|くちぶえ}を{吹|ふ}きながら: while whistling
- {口笛|くちぶえ}で{呼|よ}ぶ: to call (someone/a dog) by whistling
- {口笛|くちぶえ}が{上手|じょうず}だ: to be good at whistling
- {口笛|くちぶえ}を{吹|ふ}くのが{下手|へた}だ: to be bad at whistling

RELATED TERMS:
- {口笛|くちぶえ}: whistle (the sound or act) — the noun on its own
- {指笛|ゆびぶえ}: finger whistle — whistling by putting fingers in the mouth for a louder sound
- {笛|ふえ}を{吹|ふ}く: to play a flute/whistle — uses the same verb {吹|ふ}く
